st.headline: Japan’s exports grow at fastest pace since 2022 on chips
st.teaser: The value of exports rose 23.2 per cent in July from a year earlier.
fullText: Japan’s export growth accelerated to the fastest pace since 2022, fuelled by robust demand for chips and cars and a yen that weakened to a 40-year low.

The value of exports rose 23.2 per cent in July from a year earlier, accelerating from a 19.3 per cent gain in June, the Finance Ministry reported on Aug 20. The result compared with economists’ median forecast of a 20.1 per cent increase. It was the fastest advance since October 2022.

Imports rose 27.8 per cent, faster than the previous month’s 25.4 per cent gain and economists’ estimate of a 25.1 per cent increase. The trade deficit widened to ¥634.5 billion (S$5.09 billion) on an unadjusted basis from a revised ¥409.9 billion deficit in June, marking a third straight month in the red.

The data show that Japan’s manufacturers have largely managed to navigate the fallout from the Middle East conflict so far, an encouraging sign for Japan’s economy after growth fell short of expectations in the three months through June due to lacklustre domestic demand.
“Exports of semiconductor manufacturing equipment and semiconductor components are increasing due to the recent AI boom,” said Yuki Ito, economist at Nomura Securities Co.

Exports of chemical products also rose, he said, adding, “I suspect this is partly because supply constraints on naphtha have eased to some extent, allowing exports–which had been declining–to finally rebound.”

The weak yen boosted the value of shipments and has been a factor supporting businesses by making their products more competitive in overseas markets. The currency touched its weakest level against the dollar in 40 years in July. The yen averaged 161.83 versus the dollar, 11.2 per cent weaker than a year earlier, the ministry said.

Robust global demand for chips used in artificial intelligence was among the key drivers of the latest advance. Outbound shipments of electronic components including semiconductors increased about 49 per cent. Other gainers included shipments of passenger cars, which rose 21 per cent.
By destination, shipments to the US increased 22 per cent, while those to China and Europe climbed 25.8 per cent and 19.1 per cent, respectively.
Meanwhile, the war in Iran continued to alter Japan’s energy procurement patterns after the conflict led to the virtual closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

The trade report showed the total value of oil imports jumped nearly 88 per cent, with the volume increasing 5.5 per cent. The proportion of imports from the US rose to 36 per cent of the total by volume, from 7 per cent in February, while the proportion coming from the Mideast fell to 59 per cent.

Uncertainty surrounding the conflict persisted after a 60-day negotiation window established under a US-Iran memorandum of understanding expired on Aug 17 without a permanent peace deal. The interim agreement was aimed at resolving disputes over the Strait of Hormuz, Iran’s nuclear program and economic sanctions, but failed to produce a lasting settlement.
“Looking at the shipping data, it seems Japan has continued to make progress in securing alternative supplies from the US,” Ito said. BLOOMBERG

cna.headline: Asian stocks rally as US Treasury steps in to ease bond fears
cna.teaser: Asian stocks rally as US Treasury steps in to ease bond fears
fullText: HONG KONG: Asian markets rallied on Thursday (Aug 20) after the US Treasury said it would "at least double" the amount of long-term bonds to push down borrowing costs, after they surged this week to near two-decade highs.

The surprise move provided a much-needed shot in the arm for investors worried about a spike in 10- and 30-year yields caused by the prospect of inflation staying elevated, government borrowing and possible Federal Reserve interest rate hikes.
Soon after the announcement, US equities reversed losses to end higher while the dollar tumbled against its peers as traders breathed a sigh of relief following a fresh bout of selling.
Fears had been surging after the yield on a 30-year US Treasury on Tuesday hit its highest level since June 2007, before the global financial crisis.
"I see it as a very strong sign that the Treasury has decided higher US yields are unacceptable, and that the recent blowout in the long end is undesirable.
"Clearly, Donald (Trump) is not happy yields have blown out."
The positive mood boosted Asia, where tech firms - which rely on debt to pay for their huge AI investments - were pummelled Wednesday.
Seoul led the charge higher, having been the focus of selling pressure the day before.

The Kospi jumped more than six per cent at one point as chipmaker SK hynix rocketed more than 12 per cent, helped by Wednesday's announcement by the firm of a US$29 billion share buyback aimed at soothing recent worries. Samsung climbed almost nine per cent.
Tech firms also helped Tokyo higher, while Hong Kong, Shanghai, Sydney, Wellington and Manila were also well up.
The dollar stabilised after sinking against its peers, while gold jumped back above US$4,500 for the first time since early June.

"The key question now is whether the fall in yields can last. If oil prices remain elevated and concerns over US borrowing continue, pressure on the long end of the Treasury curve could return," said City Index's Fiona Cincotta.
Crude prices have been rising for the past two weeks as hopes for a US-Iran deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz fade - the deadline for an agreement came up this week.
Washington's naval blockade on Iran's ports and Tehran's attacks on commercial ships continue, and Iran's armed forces warned Gulf countries against assisting the US military on Wednesday.
While both sides recently said messages were being exchanged, Trump on Tuesday insisted talks were off, taunting Iran with a social media post depicting the strait as a "NEW US Territory" .
Meanwhile, minutes from the Fed's July meeting showed many policymakers believe interest rate hikes will be necessary if inflation does not decline.
Three of the 12 voting members of the Federal Open Market Committee dissented from the majority decision to hold rates steady, instead calling for an increase.
They noted economic activity had continued to expand at a "solid pace", but business investment was concentrated in the AI industry.

Eyes are now on next week's annual meeting of central bankers, economists and finance chiefs at Jackson Hole, Wyoming, where investors will be hoping for some idea about Fed boss Kevin Warsh's thinking on rates.

listening.title: Singapore's Fleet-wide Transition to Green Buses
listening.transcript: As Singapore gears up for its green transition, the Land Transport Authority has announced that half of its public bus fleet will be electric by 2030. Commuters can expect quieter rides and cleaner air as older diesel models are progressively phased out. However, deploying the necessary high-powered charging infrastructure at depots islandwide remains a complex logistical challenge.

economistArticle.title: Why bond markets are unnerving rich-world politicians
paras: While stock markets across the globe scale historic heights, a quieter, far more ominous trend is unfolding in the background. Government bond yields—the interest rates rich nations pay to borrow money—have been climbing steadily. For politicians in Washington, London, and Tokyo, this upward tick is not merely a technical financial detail. It is a stark warning that the era of cheap, boundless public debt has come to a grinding halt.

Bond yields rise when investors demand a higher return to hold sovereign debt. This typically happens when they expect persistent inflation, or when they worry that governments are borrowing too much. Recently, massive post-pandemic spending coupled with heavy subsidies for industrial policies have pushed national debts to eye-watering levels. Bond vigilantes, once thought dormant after decades of low interest rates, are waking up to demand a hefty premium.

This shift represents a political nightmare. When yields rise, a larger portion of a nation's tax revenue must be diverted toward paying interest, rather than funding public infrastructure, healthcare, or popular tax cuts. It severely restricts a politician's room for maneuver. If a newly elected leader attempts to finance grand promises through more deficits, the bond market can punish them instantly with a devastating sell-off, much like the market rebellion that doomed the short-lived British government under Liz Truss.

The consequences of this trend reach far beyond Western capitals. Higher yields in major economies exert upward pressure on borrowing costs globally, strengthening the US dollar and making international debt servicing more expensive. Open economies and financial hubs, including Singapore, closely watch these developments. Yield differentials can trigger sudden capital outflows and complicate the task of domestic central banks aiming to manage currency stability.

Ultimately, the message from the bond market is clear. Equity investors may be celebrating corporate profits, but the debt market is flashing a warning sign about long-term fiscal sustainability. Politicians can no longer take cheap money for granted; the reckoning of higher-for-longer interest rates has finally arrived.
economistArticle.cn:
在全球股市屡攀历史新高的同时，一个更为隐蔽且不祥的趋势正在后台上演。政府国债收益率（即富裕国家为借钱而支付的利率）一直在稳步攀升。对于华盛顿、伦敦和东京的政治家来说，这一上升趋势并不仅仅是一个技术性的金融细节。它是一个严厉的警告：廉价、无限的公共债务时代已戛然而止。

当投资者要求获得更高的回报以持有主权债务时，债券收益率就会上升。这通常发生在他们预期通胀会持续，或者担心政府借债过多的时候。近来，疫情后巨大的支出加上对工业政策的巨额补贴，已将国家债务推向了令人瞠目结舌的高度。在经历了数十年的低利率之后，一度被认为处于蛰伏状态的“债券卫士”（指通过抛售债券惩罚挥霍无度政府的投资者）正在觉醒，并要求获得高额溢价。

这一转变代表了政治家们的噩梦。当收益率上升时，国家税收的更大一部分必须被转用于支付利息，而不是用于资助公共基础设施、医疗保健或深受选民欢迎的减税。这严重限制了政治家的施展空间。如果一位新当选的领导人企图通过增加赤字来兑现宏伟的承诺，债券市场可以立即通过破坏性的抛售来惩罚他们，就像此前让短暂的英国莉兹·特拉斯政府倒台的市场叛乱一样。

这一趋势的后果远超西方国家首都。主要经济体的高收益率给全球借贷成本带来了上行压力，推高了美元汇率，并使国际债务偿还变得更加昂贵。包括新加坡在内的开放型经济体和金融枢纽密切关注着这些事态发展。利差可能引发突然的资金外流，并使旨在维护货币稳定的本国央行的任务变得更加复杂。

归根结底，债券市场传达的信息是明确的。股市投资者或许在庆祝企业利润，但债务市场正在对长期的财政可持续性发出警告。政治家们再也不能把廉价资金视为理所当然；‘高利率维持更久’的清算终于到来了。

gems.s: While stock markets across the globe scale historic heights, a quieter, far more ominous trend is unfolding in the background.
gems.why: This sentence uses a concessive clause starting with 'while' to create a powerful contrast between the noisy stock market rally and the quiet, dangerous movement in bond yields, successfully setting an urgent tone for the piece. 该句使用“while”引导的让步状语从句，在喧闹的股市反弹与沉寂却危险的债市异动之间建立强烈的对比，为文章奠定了紧迫的基调。

gems.s: Bond vigilantes, once thought dormant after decades of low interest rates, are waking up to demand a hefty premium.
gems.why: The use of the appositive phrase 'once thought dormant after decades of low interest rates' allows the writer to smoothly insert a crucial piece of historical context without disrupting the syntactic flow. 插入语结构“once thought dormant after decades of low interest rates”的使用，使作者能够流畅地嵌入关键的历史背景信息，而不破坏句子的整体语法结构。
